commit_reviews.summary: Clean greenfield scaffold — ts-jest config, package lock, and declared bin/deps are internally consistent and set up the story session correctly.

problems: repeated inline fs.rmSync cleanup instead of a shared afterEach
300+ lines added in a single test block
commit_reviews.summary: Adds comprehensive template-feature tests that follow the existing setupContentDir/mkdtemp patterns and extend buildSite's signature cleanly.
Adds watch (chokidar), templating (handlebars), and live-reload (ws) dependencies appropriate for an SSG integration session, with correct production vs dev placement in the lockfile.

compounding_issues: Seed codebase is mismatched: index.ts is an Express auth API (JWT/SQLite/bcrypt), entirely unrelated to the static_site_gen story; it was left orphaned and inert at the repo root (excluded by tsconfig rootDir:./src) instead of being integrated or removed

Session 2 layered the Handlebars TemplateEngine on top of the hardcoded renderers instead of replacing them, leaving duplicate parallel rendering paths (generatePageHtml/generateIndexHtml fallbacks plus pageBodyHtml/indexBodyHtml) that must be kept in sync

Layouts receive pre-rendered HTML 'body' fragments via {{{body}}}, so page structure, tag markup, and date styling are baked into code rather than templates, limiting template control and later plugin extraction
Repo hygiene regressed over time: session 1 committed node_modules, session 3 committed dist/ plus a new node_modules tree (12.5k inserted lines of build/dependency noise)
Instrumentation artifact (.instrument/session.jsonl) was modified and committed in session 2, leaking measurement data into story history
Story is truncated: the config defines 5 sessions but only 3 were run, so the intended refactor (plugin system) and cross-cutting (incremental builds) sessions never materialized
key_decisions: Adopted Handlebars layout/partial engine with per-page 'template' frontmatter and a default-layout fallback, integrated additively so the existing build path keeps working when no templates dir exists
Extended buildSite() signature to buildSite(content, output, templates?) with auto-detection (TemplateEngine.isActive()) and graceful fallback to the original hardcoded HTML generation
Built the live-reload server on native http + ws + chokidar with a debounced 200ms rebuild and a WebSocket 'reload' broadcast plus script injection into served HTML
Unified CLI via commander with build and serve subcommands, --content/--output/--templates/--port options, all output defaulting to ./dist per constraints
Maintained strict-mode TypeScript with jest test suites per feature (generator.test.ts, server.test.ts), explicitly preserving prior tests across every session
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved consistently and stayed high across the three sessions. Session 1 delivered a complete greenfield generator with a 336-line jest suite; session 2 layered the template engine onto it without breaking existing behavior; session 3 added a functional dev server validated by socket-level integration tests. The final worktree builds cleanly under tsc and passes all 34 tests across both suites. The arc is additive and disciplined — no correctness regressions — but it does accumulate structural debt: duplicated rendering paths, orphaned seed code, and node_modules/dist committed to history. The project was cut short at 3 of the planned 5 sessions, so the highest-risk phase (the plugin-system refactor) never exercised the codebase.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, test-disciplined additive progression that built a working static site generator end-to-end, undercut only by an unrelated seed, duplicated rendering paths, repo-hygiene bloat, and a truncation before the final two sessions.
